releases.name: v0.8.1 — Gemini Web waits out Google's queue; usage refresh shows current figures
releases.body:
## Fixes

- **Gemini Web waits through Google's queue.** The bundled backend is now [4.26.0-magpie.2](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/releases/tag/backend-v4.26.0-magpie.2). Chat requests time out after 180 seconds of silence by default, rather than 180 seconds of total elapsed time. Google's queue heartbeats keep the request alive, and replies that keep streaming are no longer cut off. The plugin's default Gemini Web backend wait increases to 570 seconds; explicit timeout settings still take precedence. Direct and proxied connections also have bounded connection/handshake waits. (#33, #36)
- **Usage refresh shows current figures.** When Magpie requests usage, account readings at least 30 seconds old are fetched from Google again, including usage from the Gemini app, website, and other devices. Concurrent reads are shared. Failed reads normally back off for 10 minutes, with an early retry when Magpie asks again within a minute. (#34, #35)

## Documentation

- Explain how agents can use AI Studio image models for image generation and reference images. (#32)
- Clarify the default concurrency: Gemini Web allows two requests per sign-in, AI Studio one.

## Upgrade

Install the attached `magpie-gemini-web-0.8.1.tgz` or update the plugin through your usual workflow. A running Gemini Web backend is not interrupted automatically: stop the existing managed backend (its PID is in `backend.pid` in the data directory), then the next managed startup upgrades it while preserving configuration and credentials.

## Validation

- All 212 JavaScript tests passed on the release commit.
- All 51 files in the attached package were verified against commit `b6f3cfb40a560dac5a64b422b72e7237dfb3c407`.
- Backend build provenance and platform verification are documented in the linked backend release.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/compare/v0.8.0...v0.8.1

releases.name: Optimized backend 4.26.0-magpie.2
releases.body:
Ready-to-run optimized backend for **macOS, Linux and Windows, on x64 and arm64**, built from upstream v4.26.0 with `patches/argon.patch`. The next plugin release selects these assets by default during one-click setup.

New in this backend:

- Chat requests are timed by silence, not by their whole length. Gemini Web queues a request for minutes before its first words (3.6 Flash took 48 to 393 s in our runs) and sends a 38-byte heartbeat every 60 s while it waits. The old 180 s whole-request limit cut off every request queued longer than that and retried it from the back of the queue, and the third try failed at 544 s ([#33](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/issues/33)); it also cut off replies still coming at 180 s. A try is now given up, and retried, only after Google has sent nothing for `request_timeout_sec` (180 s by default: three missed heartbeats). Page loads, uploads and other requests keep their whole-request limit.
- Direct connections to Google have their own limits: 30 s to connect, and the connection is dropped if Google sends nothing within 10 s of it opening. tls-client redials a dropped HTTP/2 connection without the request's context, so a server that accepted the connection and never answered could stall requests until the backend restarted. Proxied connections get a 10 s TLS handshake limit.

## Build provenance

- Upstream: [zexadev/gemini-web2api-go@7ce02d8](https://github.com/zexadev/gemini-web2api-go/commit/7ce02d89512058b2bd147fb2dc4e40187f5135ad)
- Patch SHA-256: `c0697c8382db912b545ed11394e67a998a55393bb1f81e86f6fb2400c150dccb`
- Go: `1.27.1`, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `-trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags="-s -w"`
- Reported backend version: `4.26.0-magpie.2`
- Included: six executables, patched source archive, `build.json`, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and the upstream MIT license.

The installer pins each executable's SHA-256 in `lib/backend-release.json`. Existing published assets must not be overwritten because installed plugin versions rely on those hashes.

## Validation

All seven jobs in [the release verification workflow](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/41279136190) passed. Each of the six native OS/architecture runners rebuilt the pinned sources, passed Go tests, matched the published SHA-256, and installed and started its real executable with isolated data, including the proxy-binding check. The plugin's 211 JavaScript tests passed. These checks used no Google credentials.

Live checks on one account: with silence timing, requests queued for 393 s and 188 s were answered (the longest silence while queued was about 60 s). An anonymous page load from gemini.google.com through the new dialer worked over HTTP/2, including after a forced redial.

## Upgrade and rollback

A running backend is left alone. Stop it before upgrading (the managed process ID is in the data directory's `backend.pid`); the next automatic start upgrades a stopped official backend and keeps configuration, credentials and the account database.

From the plugin directory, with the backend stopped:

```bash
npm run backend:install           # select this optimized release
npm run backend:install:upstream  # select the pinned official v4.26.0
```

The selected channel persists across automatic starts. Failed downloads or checksum verification preserve the existing binary.

releases.name: v0.8.0 — AI Studio image generation, image input, and AI Studio 0.2.18
releases.body:
Draws images with Google AI Studio's Nano Banana models in Magpie, reads images in AI Studio chats by default, and upgrades the managed AI Studio backend to v0.2.18 (`0.2.18-magpie.1`) with SpiderMonkey WAA.

- **Image generation with AI Studio** (#28): the account's Nano Banana image models (`gemini-3.1-flash-image`, `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image`, `gemini-3-pro-image`, `gemini-nano-banana-2.1`, `gemini-2.5-flash-image`) appear among Magpie's image models, so Automatic, the `generate_image` tool and `magpie tool generate_image` can draw with them. Magpie's aspect ratio is asked as `imageConfig.aspectRatio` (the nearest one each model takes). Turn it off with `studio.imageModels: false`. **Needs Magpie v0.1.2075 or later**; older Magpie only lists these models in chat.
- **Image input on by default for AI Studio** (#30): AI Studio's chat models read the images and screenshots in a chat without setting `allowImages`. Gemini Web keeps it off by default (`gemini-3.6-flash` there timed out with images). `studio.allowImages: false` or a top-level `allowImages: false` turns it off.
- **AI Studio 0.2.18-magpie.1** ([release](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/releases/tag/studio-v0.2.18-magpie.1)) (#31): based on upstream v0.2.18 (`9b694a6b7c6439db1767a577994dfcc87a3cf588`). Upstream removed the pure Go (goja) WAA backend, so generation's WAA now runs on SpiderMonkey (`WAA_BACKEND=spidermonkey`), still inside the service with no browser; Camoufox is only for Google sign-in. Upstream fixes include re-login only when an account is really signed out, re-uploading deleted inline attachments, and continuing when thinking fills the output cap.
  - Upstream's new `-search` model copies (`SEARCH_MODEL_ALIASES`) stay off unless turned on in the admin page, so Magpie doesn't list most models twice. Its other new settings keep what the admin page saves.
  - A refused key on Gemini's API (400 `API_KEY_INVALID`, or 403 with no key) asks for a sign-in again; Google's own 403 is passed on as it came.
- Fix a Windows-only race in a service restart test (#29).

### Upgrading notes

- On the next managed start, an older managed backend is stopped and replaced by `0.2.18-magpie.1`, keeping accounts, port, settings and databases. The request-body migration from 0.2.17 still applies to setups that skipped it.
- First-time download size for the managed AI Studio service is ~40 MB (previously ~30 MB).
- Not verified in this release: a new Google sign-in through the Camoufox login window (the live check used an account that was already signed in).

Validation: [AI Studio verification](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/41040252240) at the release commit and [PR #31 verification](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/41038083289) passed on all five native runners; 210 plugin tests pass; the public `studio-v0.2.18-magpie.1` archive installs from GitHub and passes the managed smoke test; live Google AI Studio text, streaming, image input and image generation passed with a signed-in account.

releases.name: AI Studio 0.2.18-magpie.1
releases.body:
AI Studio backend based on upstream v0.2.18, managed exclusively by the Magpie plugin.

- **WAA on SpiderMonkey**: upstream v0.2.18 removed the pure Go (goja) WAA backend; this build runs `WAA_BACKEND=spidermonkey`, Firefox's JS engine linked in through CGO. Generation still needs no browser; Camoufox is only for Google sign-in.
- Built with upstream's distributor settings (`-X internal/app.version=v0.2.18-magpie.1`, `-X internal/app.managedBy=magpie-gemini-web`). Update checks return local managed status without contacting GitHub; installing an update returns HTTP 409 without changing files or restarting.
- Links upstream's prebuilt SpiderMonkey static libraries (`Mag1cFall/firefox` release `v152.0.4-aistudio2api.1`), pinned per target by SHA-256. On Linux (musl, static), mozglue's environment interposers are removed from `libjs_static.a`: they look up libc's `setenv` and the rest with `dlsym(RTLD_NEXT)`, which a static executable can't resolve, and crash on purpose.
- Safe request-body migration (`patches/studio-0.2.17-preserve-request-bodies.patch`, SHA-256 `4cdafbe2c1fb9c2fa913c15845257e0a16bbfa406fb7dc11d0a5bf1eaaa996a0`), still needed: upstream v0.2.18 still drops the legacy `bodies` table.
- Includes five SHA-256-pinned platform archives, upstream MIT license, checksums, and reproducible build metadata (`-buildid=`, Zig 0.16.0 musl static on Linux, llvm-mingw 20261020 UCRT on Windows linking the Linux archive's target libraries on every builder, Xcode 26.3 on macOS). Archives are 36–39 MB.

Source: upstream commit `9b694a6b7c6439db1767a577994dfcc87a3cf588` (tag v0.2.18) + `studio-0.2.17-preserve-request-bodies.patch`. Go 1.27.1, Node v26.8.2, Camoufox 152.0.4-beta.29, SpiderMonkey v152.0.4-aistudio2api.1. Build instructions: `docs/studio-release.md`.

Validation: all five native runners in [the verification workflow](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/41040252240) rebuilt the pinned source at the release commit, matched the archive and executable SHA-256, installed the real archive with isolated data (SpiderMonkey WAA, no `-search` copies), verified legacy request-body migration across restart, confirmed managed update status and HTTP 409 on update, and passed the plugin tests with that archive. Linux and Windows archives also match a macOS arm64 cross-build byte for byte. A live check with a signed-in account (text, streaming, image input, image generation) passed on the darwin-arm64 archive.

These are backend assets consumed by the magpie-gemini-web plugin release, not the npm plugin package.

releases.name: v0.7.0 — AI Studio 0.2.17, safe body migration, and Twin Sparkles icon
releases.body:
Upgrades the managed Google AI Studio backend to v0.2.17 (`0.2.17-magpie.1`) and adds the Twin Sparkles plugin icon.

- **AI Studio 0.2.17-magpie.1** ([release](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/releases/tag/studio-v0.2.17-magpie.1)): based on upstream v0.2.17 (`bd6c40f5f8a3a680a19a1ebff67216298d8bae27`), which switches to native SQLite (`mattn/go-sqlite3`, WAL, incremental vacuum, busy timeout) and adds video inputs, multi-account `authuser` session discovery, dynamic `thinking_levels`, and first-event hedging.
- **Safe request-body migration**: upstream v0.2.17 replaces the plaintext `bodies` table with a compressed `request_bodies` table; `patches/studio-0.2.17-preserve-request-bodies.patch` compresses and migrates pre-0.2.17 rows in a transaction before dropping the legacy table.
- **Dynamic reasoning efforts**: `listStudioModels` now derives model variants from upstream's `thinking_levels` catalog metadata (`minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`), falling back to the previous defaults for older external servers.
- **Saved `FIRST_EVENT_HEDGE` preserved**: `FIRST_EVENT_HEDGE` is kept across `.env` rewrites while isolating any host environment variable of the same name.
- **Reproducible CGO builds across builders**: C toolchains are pinned in `lib/studio-release.json` (Zig 0.16.0 musl static on Linux, llvm-mingw 20261020 UCRT on Windows, Xcode 26.3 on macOS) and built with `-ldflags=-buildid=`.
- **Twin Sparkles plugin icon** (#25, #26).

### Upgrading notes

- A running backend is left alone; once it is stopped, the next start installs `0.2.17-magpie.1` and preserves accounts, settings, and databases.
- **Database migration is one-way**: first startup migrates and vacuums existing SQLite databases. Back up the data directory (`~/.local/share/magpie-ai-studio`) before upgrading if you may need to downgrade to 0.2.16.
- First-time download size for the managed AI Studio service is ~30 MB (previously ~25 MB).

Validation: [AI Studio verification](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/40816292207) and [PR #27 verification](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/40812596486) passed on all five native runners; 207 plugin tests pass; live end-to-end Google AI Studio generation, multi-turn tool calling, cancellation, and auto-restart passed.
